newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Swiss panel chides PTT on Internet practice.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swiss panel chides PTT on Internet practice.

text.p: The Swiss Cartel Commission said on Friday the state-owned Telecom PTT authority violated competitive practices when it started its Internet service last year, a ruling the telecoms carrier vowed to contest.

At least one leading Swiss private Internet provider said it believed Telecom PTT still had a competitive advantage in the domestic market for Internet services, worth an estimated 350 million Swiss francs ($250 million) a year in subscriber and user fees.

The Cartel Commission said in a statement that a probe, begun after Telecom PTT started its Internet access provider Blue Window last September, showed violations occured but had since ceased, making further action unnecessary.

"The Commission maintains that there was discrimination taking place, and it requires that the Telecom PTT refrain in future from such practice. The Telecom PTT has already altered its practice during the course of investigations, so that today no further violations exist," the competiton panel said.

Commission vice president Roland von Bueren said the PTT had altered its strategy to make its service less costly, setting up "points of presence" (POPs), dial-up points Internet subscribers can access at cheaper rates than direct long-distance rates.
He said the original business plan foresaw Blue Window racking up a loss of 100 million Swiss francs for the year 2002 alone, adding such projections led to the plan being changed.
The Cartel Commission also said that, based on its decision, private providers may seek to claim damages in civil court.
The PTT said it will contest the decision on principle.

"Telecom PTT vigorously rejects the accusation that, with its online service Blue Window, it discriminated against private Internet providers and thus violated the cartel laws," it said in a statement.
According to the cartel authorities, the telecoms provider temporarily created an unfair advantage by providing Internet access based on cheaper local telephone charges via its access number 0-842.
The commission said Telecom failed to give its rivals adequate information about access to the number. This forced them to charge subscribers more expensive long-distance rates.
But the PTT said the private providers have had access to the 0-842 number on the same terms as Telecom PTT.
"In spite of that, none have used it," it added.
Telecom PTT, slated for privatisation in 1998, also contested allegations Blue Window is not commercially viable.

Private Internet providers said the Swiss Federal Court had issued a preliminary decision in favour of the state-owned PTT in a similar case. Private providers say they are still hoping a final decision will rule in their favour.
Guenter Nierlich, spokesman for a rival service, Swiss Online AG, said that it welcomed the Cartel Commission decision, but that further measures were needed.
"Measures to redress the competitive distortions are urgently needed and expected by Swiss Online," Nierlich said.
He said private providers still did not know the location of the PTT's POP links, putting them at a disadvantage. ($ = 1.434 Swiss Francs)
